evidence_quotes.two_concerns_question: Never asked. Customer mentioned divorce context ('going through divorce') but Jules never probed concerns systematically.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: No follow-up on the divorce concern or any other customer concern raised.
evidence_quotes.value_days: Jules quoted 8:30-9:00 AM start but never offered Value Days or asked about date flexibility for cheaper alternatives.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_then_ask: No rate lock, no deposit statement. Jules moved straight to scheduling with 'I'll get this scheduled we're going to be arriving around 8:30 to nine in the morning tomorrow' and never asked 'Would you like our help with your move?' Kurt booked because he needed the service urgently, not because Jules asked for it.

top_strength: Jules quickly confirmed availability, gathered all essential logistics (addresses, furniture inventory, wardrobe box count, fragile items, story count), and delivered a concrete estimate with materials cost range, enabling an immediate booking on a time-sensitive move.
coaching_note: Jules skipped the entire discovery bookend (step 2's two-concerns question and the need to understand what actually worries this customer) and went straight to logistics, missing the chance to connect the promises (on-time guarantee, damage coverage) to what matters most to Kurt, especially given the emotional context of the divorce.
